## Interfaces

Order refs and tags: see Identifier walkthrough. Trading fields used are `client_order_ref`, `client_position_ref` and `client_tags`.

## Identifier walkthrough

- Generated by: the basket worker (never the API process, never trading)
- Generated when: when the leg's order_intent row is created, in the same transaction that commits the holdings version, before any call to trading
- Verified: NO — spike S2 confirms trading accepts the ":" separator and a ref of about 90 characters

| Part | Why |
|---|---|
| basket_id | A UUID, so refs never collide across baskets, and it groups every order of a basket for reconciliation |
| purpose (none, t<n>, r<k>, x) | Separate namespaces so top-up n, roll k and exit never collide with the initial order for the same market |
| market_id | Identifies the leg, so one live ref exists per leg |
| attempt | Lets a leg be re-placed after a terminal rejection, because a repeated ref would return the rejected order forever |

| Scenario | Ref used | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| First send of a leg | basket:market:1 | Trading creates the order |
| Crash after commit, before send | basket:market:1 (stored) | Worker re-sends the stored body on restart; one order |
| Crash after send, answer lost | basket:market:1 (stored) | Trading returns the order it already holds; no duplicate |
| Terminal rejection | basket:market:2 | A new order; the rejected one stays dead |
| Same ref, changed body | basket:market:1 | Trading answers 409 and the worker raises an alert |

## Data flow

The worker sends POST /v1/orders and, on timeout or an unknown outcome, retries with the same ref and stored body; only a terminal rejection starts the next attempt.

## Decisions

- DEC-0548 — persist the order request before sending, because a crash between deciding and sending would otherwise lose or duplicate the order.
- DEC-0554 — build refs from stable business keys, because a random ref cannot be reproduced after a crash and defeats deduplication.
- DEC-0555 — advance the attempt only on terminal rejection, so that a retry after an unknown outcome can never create a second venue order.
